item.title: Beyond AI Adoption: People Management, Work Design and Sustainable Performance in AI-Enabled Organisations
item.content:encoded:
AI systems are increasingly used in HR functions such as recruitment, employee analytics, training, performance management and workforce planning. While organizations often expect these systems to improve efficiency and fairness, they raise concerns about transparency, employee wellbeing, job quality and whether such systems genuinely enhance organizational performance. This special issue shifts focus from simply whether organizations adopt AI to how AI-enabled HR systems should be designed, governed and experienced to benefit employees and organizational effectiveness.

The special issue examines the relationship between AI-enabled HR practices and sustainable organizational performance, considering both potential benefits and risks. It invites research exploring when and how AI strengthens or undermines work quality, fairness, employee voice, inclusion and capability development. The collection addresses emerging regulatory interest from bodies like the OECD and EU AI Act, which recognize that AI in employment decisions requires responsible governance.

Appel publié par Journal of Organizational Effectiveness: People and Performance. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-enabled recruitment, selection and fair access to work: How AI screening, automated assessments, candidate ranking, video interviews and people analytics affect fairness, validity, transparency, accessibility and selection outcomes.
  • AI-supported training, development and capability building: How AI-enabled learning systems, skills analytics, career platforms and talent systems affect reskilling, development access, career visibility and employee capability.
  • AI-enabled performance management, monitoring and evaluation: How algorithmic monitoring, datafication and AI-supported appraisal affect fairness, trust, employee agency, wellbeing, reasonable adjustment and performance outcomes.
  • Work design, job quality and employee voice in AI-enabled workplaces: How AI changes autonomy, workload, coordination, meaningful work, participation, consultation and human oversight in people-management decisions.
  • Inclusion, disability, governance and sustainable organisational effectiveness: How organisations design AI-enabled HRM systems that reduce bias, support EDI, protect disabled workers and applicants, strengthen trust and contribute to sustainable organisational performance.

Timeline

  • June 25, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • January 25, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Responsible Design: Care Ethics for AI-Enabled Systems
item.content:encoded:
Fernando Miramontes Forattini, Dublin City University

Regina Connolly, Dublin City University

This special issue examines how care ethics and relational approaches can advance responsible design and governance of AI-enabled systems. While contemporary AI ethics discourse has focused on fairness, transparency, and compliance frameworks, this call seeks to address the structural, relational, and institutional dimensions of how digital systems affect vulnerability, participation, and human agency.

The special issue invites empirical research, conceptual contributions, design science research, and interdisciplinary perspectives that move beyond procedural approaches to explore responsibility distribution across socio-technical arrangements. Submissions should examine relationships between technology, power, participation, exclusion, and accountability in digital environments, grounded in diverse epistemological and methodological traditions.

Appel publié par Information Systems Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Consumer Vulnerability in the Age of Algorithmic Persuasion: Risks, Responsibilities, and Remedies
item.content:encoded:
Jenny Le, VinUniversity

Helen Chun, Cornell University

Sara Quach, Griffith University

Park Thaichon, University of Southern Queensland

This Special Issue aims to advance ethics of algorithmic persuasion in marketing. It seeks to fill the critical gaps related to the underexplored mechanisms by which AI technologies construct, amplify, or mitigate consumer vulnerability; the limited empirical evidence on how privacy risks intersect with persuasion strategies; and the insufficient integration of ethical principles into the design of AI-powered marketing systems.

Appel publié par Journal of Consumer Behaviour. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mechanisms by which AI technologies construct, amplify, or mitigate consumer vulnerability
  • Privacy risks and their intersection with persuasion strategies
  • Ethical principles in the design of AI-powered marketing systems
  • Ethics of algorithmic persuasion in marketing

Timeline

  • July 1, 2027: Submission window opens
  • August 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Human-AI Interaction in Intelligent Workplaces: Behaviour, Trust, Experience, and Human-Centered Design
item.content:encoded:
Muhammad Imran Rasheed, University of Surrey

Barbara Rita Barricelli, Università degli Studi di Brescia

Waseem Ul Hameed, Universiti Utara Malaysia

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence systems are transforming workplace interactions, employee behavior, and organizational dynamics. While prior research has focused on AI adoption and performance outcomes, this collection addresses the human-centered dimensions of AI at work, including how employees develop trust in intelligent systems, experience AI-mediated processes, adapt their behaviors, and navigate issues such as technostress, autonomy, and cognitive load.

The special issue prioritizes behavioral, cognitive, and psychological perspectives on human-AI interaction in organizational settings. It seeks contributions that explore employee experiences with intelligent technologies, design of user-centered AI systems, transparency mechanisms, and the creation of psychologically sustainable digital work environments. The collection welcomes empirical, theoretical, and design-oriented research across quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method approaches.
